summary: A member can release old envelope payloads locally: once an envelope is 14 days old, alone in its batch, holds only valid records, carries no fleet, principal, pairing, daemon.started or other member's message.sent claim, is not its writer's newest, and every claim of it carries its writer's signature by a key membership admits, its payload, envelope signatures, hold and valid records are deleted and its identity stays in released_envelopes. Readers, inventories and digests do not change. The pass ships switched off (ENVELOPE_RELEASE) until the claim-set transport can serve released claims

replay.detail: No replay. Readers that find a claim's envelope by its batch (admission, the record view, the self-writer, writer and pairing signer checks, sealing, record repairs and the local trim capture and delete) read stored and released envelopes alike. For a released envelope the signer checks accept the claim's own writer signature (claim_member_signatures) by the key membership admits for that writer and sequence; the envelope signature path is unchanged for stored envelopes. Readers of payloads (export, backup, wire archive, signature migration and backfill, rename proofs) skip released envelopes. The scoped capture's record counts and late-claim checks seek their own indexes instead of running the record view in full for each claim and writer.

schema.detail: New table released_envelopes (identity, previous hash, accepted time, batch, original rowid, release time; indexes on batch_id and a unique one on original_rowid) and view envelope_rows (stored and released envelopes, by row_id). The view replica_record_rows gains a branch for released envelopes and is replaced on open when its definition differs. The inventory trigger replica_envelopes_inventory_DELETE_v2 is replaced by _v3, which also leaves a released envelope's deletion uncounted. New meta key envelope_release_cursor. No storage version change; nothing is written to the new table while the pass is off.

rules.detail: No checkpoint rule or fleet coordination change. A local cut drops a released envelope's claims as it would a stored one's, and its tombstone then stands for the identity.

compatibility.detail: No wire or API change. A released envelope stays in this member's replication inventory without its payload, as a checkpoint tombstone does, so the authority digest is unchanged and peers never send it again; admission refuses it if one does. This member no longer serves it: a peer that lacks it cannot get it here until the claim-set transport, which is why the pass is off.

downtime.detail: No startup work beyond creating the table, view and replaced trigger and view in the opening transaction. When a later release switches the pass on, it reads envelopes in rowid order, at most 512 and 10 ms of writer work a page, then gives the freed pages back 128 at a time.

recovery.detail: Rollback to the previous release is supported while the pass is off: released_envelopes is empty, the previous release keeps this build's replica_record_rows definition (it creates the view only when missing), which reads the same rows while nothing is released, and it recreates replica_envelopes_inventory_DELETE_v2 beside _v3, so a deletion both count moves the inventory generation twice, which only rebuilds a snapshot that was rebuilt anyway. Once a later release has released envelopes, the previous release would not find their claims admitted or their records; that release's note states the floor.
